nodes.label: einops rearrange
nodes.plain: Name the axes on both sides of an arrow and einops works out the transpose/reshape for you.
nodes.title: Relabel the shelves, never the jars

nodes.label: einops reduce
nodes.plain: A named-axis mean/sum/max: the axes you drop from the right-hand side are the ones reduced over.
nodes.title: Cross off a label, pour the shelf

nodes.label: einops repeat
nodes.plain: Adds a new named axis by copying along it — broadcasting you can read.
nodes.title: A photocopier with a collate switch

nodes.label: einsum
nodes.plain: Write the index letters of both inputs and the output; repeated letters are summed over.
nodes.title: The one-line tensor contract

nodes.label: Broadcasting
nodes.plain: Trailing dimensions of size 1 are stretched to match; anything else is an error.
nodes.title: Line up right, mirror the ones

nodes.label: Ray generation
nodes.plain: Build a batch of rays as (origin, direction) pairs laid out on a grid — a tensor-construction exercise wearing a graphics costume.
nodes.title: Every torch gets a stand-and-aim card

nodes.label: Ray–object intersection
nodes.plain: Solving a small linear system per ray to find where it hits a segment or triangle.
nodes.title: Where the two walkers meet

nodes.label: Barycentric coordinates
nodes.plain: A point is inside a triangle iff its three weights are all non-negative and sum to one.
nodes.title: Where does the tray balance?

nodes.label: Batched raytracing
nodes.plain: Do every ray against every triangle at once by adding batch axes instead of writing a loop.
nodes.title: A clerk at every desk

nodes.label: Strides
nodes.plain: A tensor is a flat block of memory plus a (size, stride) rule that turns indices into offsets.
nodes.title: One street, many directions cards

nodes.label: as_strided & stride tricks
nodes.plain: Write the stride rule yourself and you get sliding windows for free, with no copy.
nodes.title: New routes down the same street

nodes.label: Convolution
nodes.plain: Slide one small weight tensor over the input and take a dot product at every position.
nodes.title: One stencil, slid everywhere

nodes.label: Padding
nodes.plain: Ring the input with a constant so the output keeps the size you want.
nodes.title: A blank margin so the stamp fits

nodes.label: Max pooling
nodes.plain: Downsample by taking the largest value in each window — no parameters, just a stride-2 view and a max.
nodes.title: Only the loudest in each square

nodes.label: Linear layer
nodes.plain: A learned matrix multiply plus a bias; the unit every other module is assembled from.
nodes.title: A mixing desk of learned faders

nodes.label: BatchNorm2d
nodes.plain: Normalise each channel over the batch during training, then use running statistics at eval time.
nodes.title: Grade the class, remember the curve

nodes.label: Residual block
nodes.plain: Add the block's input to its output so gradients have a path that skips the block entirely.
nodes.title: Pencil notes, never retype the page

nodes.label: ResNet34
nodes.plain: A stack of block groups assembled from your own modules, then loaded with real pretrained weights.
nodes.title: Right seats, right sheet music

nodes.label: SGD
nodes.plain: Step downhill: subtract the learning rate times the gradient.
nodes.title: Feel the slope, take a stride

nodes.label: Momentum
nodes.plain: Keep a running average of past gradients and step along that instead, so consistent directions accumulate.
nodes.title: The heavy ball in the ravine

nodes.label: RMSprop
nodes.plain: Divide each parameter's step by the square root of a running average of its squared gradients.
nodes.title: Level each channel by its own loudness

nodes.label: Adam
nodes.plain: Keep a running mean and a running variance per parameter and step by mean over root-variance, so every parameter gets its own effective learning rate.
nodes.title: Every weight gets its own ruler

nodes.label: AdamW vs Adam
nodes.plain: Adam with weight decay decoupled — the decay is applied straight to the weights, not through the adaptive denominator.
nodes.title: Take the tax out of the envelope

nodes.label: Weight decay
nodes.plain: Shrink every weight a little each step; an L2 penalty applied by the optimiser rather than the loss.
nodes.title: A rubber band back to zero

nodes.label: Learning-rate schedule
nodes.plain: Change the learning rate over training — warm up, then anneal.
nodes.title: Jog out, run, then walk in

nodes.label: Weights & Biases sweeps
nodes.plain: Log every run, then let a sweep search the hyperparameter space instead of you.
nodes.title: Nine random holes beat a grid

nodes.label: Distributed data parallel
nodes.plain: Give every GPU a slice of the batch, average the gradients with an all-reduce, and every copy of the model steps identically.
nodes.title: Taste apart, adjust together

nodes.label: Computational graph
nodes.plain: The forward pass records which tensors made which, so the backward pass has a route to walk.
nodes.title: Every bowl remembers its recipe

nodes.label: Backward function
nodes.plain: Each op stores how to turn 'gradient w.r.t. my output' into 'gradient w.r.t. each of my inputs'.
nodes.title: An exchange booth at every step

nodes.label: Topological sort
nodes.plain: Order the graph so no node is visited before everything that depends on it.

nodes.label: Backprop & topological order
nodes.plain: Walk the graph in reverse topological order, applying each backward function and summing where a tensor was used more than once.
nodes.title: Pass the blame back, add it up

nodes.label: Unbroadcast
nodes.plain: Because a broadcast copies a tensor forward, the backward pass has to sum the gradient back down to the original shape.
nodes.title: Many prints, one stamp to fix

nodes.label: Cross-entropy loss
nodes.plain: Negative log-probability of the correct token, computed straight from logits for numerical stability.

nodes.label: Autoencoder
nodes.plain: Squeeze the input through a narrow bottleneck and reconstruct it; the bottleneck is forced to be a compressed code.
nodes.title: A telegram with a word limit

nodes.label: Latent space
nodes.plain: The coordinates the bottleneck learns; interpolating between two of them should give plausible outputs.

nodes.label: VAE
nodes.plain: An autoencoder whose encoder outputs a distribution, trained to keep that distribution close to a standard normal.

nodes.label: Reparameterisation trick
nodes.plain: Sample as mean + sigma × noise so the gradient can flow through the sampling step.

nodes.label: KL divergence
nodes.plain: How far one distribution is from another, in nats; zero only when they are identical.

nodes.label: GAN
nodes.plain: Train a generator against a discriminator; each one's loss is the other's success.

nodes.label: Tokenization
nodes.plain: Text becomes integer ids from a fixed vocabulary, and the split is rarely where you'd put it.

nodes.label: Embedding
nodes.plain: A lookup table turning each token id into a vector in the residual stream.

nodes.label: Positional embedding
nodes.plain: A learned vector added per position, because attention itself has no notion of order.

nodes.label: LayerNorm
nodes.plain: Centre and rescale each token's residual vector, then apply a learned gain and bias.

nodes.label: Residual stream
nodes.plain: A shared bus every component reads from and writes to by addition, so the whole model is a sum of contributions.

nodes.label: Attention head
nodes.plain: One head moves information from earlier positions to the current one, choosing where by a query–key match and what by a value–output map.

nodes.label: Softmax attention & the causal mask
nodes.plain: Scale the query–key scores by 1/sqrt(d_head), mask out future positions with negative infinity, then softmax over keys.

nodes.label: MLP layer
nodes.plain: Two linear maps with a non-linearity between them, applied to each position independently.

nodes.label: GELU
nodes.plain: The smooth non-linearity transformers use in the MLP.

nodes.label: Transformer block
nodes.plain: Attention then MLP, each wrapped in LayerNorm and each writing back into the residual stream.

nodes.label: Unembedding
nodes.plain: The final matrix turning a residual vector into logits over the vocabulary.

nodes.label: KV cache
nodes.plain: Store past keys and values so generating token n+1 doesn't recompute the whole prefix.

nodes.label: Training loop
nodes.plain: Batch, forward, loss, backward, step, log — and a validation pass that tells you whether any of it worked.

nodes.label: Sampling
nodes.plain: Turning a distribution over next tokens into an actual token — the step where all the decoding knobs live.

nodes.label: Temperature
nodes.plain: Divide the logits before the softmax: below 1 sharpens the distribution, above 1 flattens it.

nodes.label: Top-k sampling
nodes.plain: Keep only the k most likely tokens, renormalise, and sample from those.

nodes.label: Top-p (nucleus) sampling
nodes.plain: Keep the smallest set of tokens whose probabilities sum past p.

nodes.label: Beam search
nodes.plain: Keep the n best partial sequences at every step instead of committing to one.

nodes.label: TransformerLens
nodes.plain: A library that loads real models with named, interpretable weights and lets you reach inside a forward pass.

nodes.label: Hooks
nodes.plain: Functions attached to a named activation that can read it, or return a modified version to replace it.

nodes.label: Activation cache
nodes.plain: Run the model once with caching on and get a dictionary of every intermediate tensor by name.

nodes.label: Attention pattern
nodes.plain: The (query, key) probability matrix for one head — the picture you look at first when asking what a head does.

nodes.label: Ablation
nodes.plain: Delete a component — zero it, or replace it with its mean — and see how much performance you lose.

nodes.label: Induction head
nodes.plain: A head implementing 'I saw A then B earlier, I'm at A again, so predict B' — it attends to the token after the previous copy of the current token.

nodes.label: Previous-token head
nodes.plain: A head that attends one position back, writing 'the token before me was X' into the residual stream.

nodes.label: Duplicate-token head
nodes.plain: A head that attends from a token back to earlier copies of the same token.

nodes.label: Induction score
nodes.plain: Average attention paid to the (offset by one) diagonal on a repeated random sequence — a number that ranks every head.

nodes.label: Circuit
nodes.plain: A small subgraph of heads and MLPs that, together, implements one identifiable behaviour.

nodes.label: QK circuit
nodes.plain: The composed matrix W_E W_Q W_K^T W_E^T that says which source tokens a head wants to attend to.

nodes.label: OV circuit
nodes.plain: The composed matrix W_E W_V W_O W_U that says what a head writes to the logits once it attends somewhere.

nodes.label: K-composition
nodes.plain: A later head's keys are built from an earlier head's output, so the two compose into one algorithm.

nodes.label: Q-composition
nodes.plain: A later head's queries are built from an earlier head's output.

nodes.label: Composition score
nodes.plain: A normalised Frobenius measure of how much one head's output subspace overlaps another head's input subspace.

nodes.label: Logit lens
nodes.plain: Apply the unembedding to an intermediate residual vector and read what the model would have said if it stopped there.

nodes.label: Direct logit attribution
nodes.plain: Project each component's write onto the logit-difference direction to get its signed contribution to the answer.

nodes.label: Factored matrix
nodes.plain: Keep a low-rank product as its two factors so you can take its SVD and norms without ever materialising the big matrix.

nodes.label: Linear probe
nodes.plain: Train a small linear classifier on frozen activations to test whether a property is linearly readable there.

nodes.label: PCA of activations
nodes.plain: Take the top principal directions of a set of activations to see whether the structure you care about is already visible.

nodes.label: Probe-directed intervention
nodes.plain: Push activations along a probe's direction and check the behaviour moves — the causal test a correlational probe can't give you.

nodes.label: Function vector
nodes.plain: A vector extracted from in-context-learning forward passes that, added to a zero-shot prompt, makes the model perform the task anyway.

nodes.label: Steering vector
nodes.plain: The difference between activations on two contrasting prompts, added back into the stream to push behaviour one way.

nodes.label: Steering hook
nodes.plain: The forward hook that actually adds a vector at a chosen layer and position range during generation.

nodes.label: Activation oracle
nodes.plain: An LLM trained to take another model's activations as input and answer arbitrary questions about them in plain English.

nodes.label: Model diffing
nodes.plain: Compare two models' activations on the same input to find what fine-tuning actually changed.

nodes.label: Indirect object identification (IOI)
nodes.plain: The behaviour where 'John and Mary went to the shops, John gave a bag to' is completed with ' Mary' — a task small enough to reverse-engineer completely.

nodes.label: Logit difference
nodes.plain: Use logit(correct) minus logit(distractor) as the metric, because it cancels everything the two share.

nodes.label: Activation patching
nodes.plain: Run on a corrupted prompt, splice one activation in from the clean run, and measure how much of the correct behaviour returns.

nodes.label: Denoising vs noising
nodes.plain: Denoising patches clean activations into a corrupted run and asks what is sufficient; noising does the reverse and asks what is necessary.

nodes.label: Path patching
nodes.plain: Patch an activation but let only one downstream route see the change, so you measure an edge rather than a node.

nodes.label: Name-mover head
nodes.plain: A late head that attends to the non-duplicated name and copies it into the logits.

nodes.label: S-inhibition head
nodes.plain: A middle-layer head that marks the duplicated name so later heads avoid attending to it.

nodes.label: Backup name-mover head
nodes.plain: A head that takes over the name-moving job when the primary name movers are ablated.

nodes.label: Minimality & faithfulness
nodes.plain: Tests that the circuit you propose is both enough to do the task and has no spare parts.

nodes.label: Transcoder
nodes.plain: An SAE-shaped model that learns the MLP's input-to-output map sparsely, rather than reconstructing one activation.

nodes.label: Attribution graph
nodes.plain: Build a graph over active latents by taking gradients between them, then prune it to the part that matters.

nodes.label: Circuit pruning
nodes.plain: Score nodes and edges by influence on the output and drop the ones below threshold.

nodes.label: Feature
nodes.plain: A direction in activation space that corresponds to something a human can name.

nodes.label: Linear representation hypothesis
nodes.plain: Models represent concepts as directions, so a concept can be read out by a projection and edited by an addition.

nodes.label: Superposition
nodes.plain: A layer represents more features than it has dimensions by storing them as non-orthogonal directions and paying interference as the cost.

nodes.label: Polysemanticity
nodes.plain: One neuron fires for several unrelated things, so reading neurons one at a time doesn't work.

nodes.label: Feature sparsity
nodes.plain: Most features are absent from most inputs, which is exactly the condition that makes superposition worth it to the model.

nodes.label: Interference
nodes.plain: Because superposed features aren't orthogonal, activating one leaks a little into the others.

nodes.label: Feature dimensionality
nodes.plain: How much of a dimension a feature gets to itself — the measure that makes the geometric arrangements legible as numbers.

nodes.label: Sparse autoencoder (SAE)
nodes.plain: A wide, sparsely-activating autoencoder trained to reconstruct an activation as a sum of a few dictionary directions.

nodes.label: SAE latent
nodes.plain: One dictionary entry: an encoder direction that detects it and a decoder direction that writes it back.

nodes.label: L1 sparsity penalty
nodes.plain: The term that pushes most latents to zero — the single dial that trades reconstruction against interpretability.

nodes.label: Dead latent
nodes.plain: A latent that never fires, wasting dictionary capacity — usually fixed by resampling it onto badly-reconstructed inputs.

nodes.label: Gated SAE
nodes.plain: Split the decision of whether a latent fires from how strongly, so the L1 penalty stops shrinking magnitudes.

nodes.label: JumpReLU SAE
nodes.plain: Use a learned per-latent threshold with a straight-through gradient estimator instead of a plain ReLU.

nodes.label: Max activating examples
nodes.plain: Run a corpus, keep the inputs where a latent fires hardest, and read them to guess what it means.

nodes.label: Autointerp
nodes.plain: Have a language model write an explanation of a latent from its top examples, then score the explanation by whether it predicts activations on held-out text.

nodes.label: Direct feature attribution
nodes.plain: Attribute a latent's activation back to the source positions an attention head read from.

nodes.label: Attribution patching
nodes.plain: A gradient-based linear approximation to patching, cheap enough to run over every latent at once.

nodes.label: SAE steering
nodes.plain: Clamp or add a specific latent during generation to test whether it causes the behaviour you think it means.

nodes.label: Algorithmic-task interpretability
nodes.plain: Reverse-engineer a tiny model on a task with known ground truth, so you can check whether your technique found the right answer.

nodes.label: Grokking
nodes.plain: Test loss stays flat long after train loss has bottomed out, then suddenly drops — memorisation being replaced by an algorithm.

nodes.label: Fourier basis analysis
nodes.plain: Change basis to sines and cosines over the input, and a dense weight matrix turns out to be sparse.

nodes.label: Progress measure
nodes.plain: A metric derived from the hypothesised circuit that moves during training even when the loss doesn't.

nodes.label: OthelloGPT
nodes.plain: A transformer trained only to predict legal Othello moves, used as a testbed for whether models build world models.

nodes.label: Emergent world representation
nodes.plain: A model trained on a surface task turns out to compute the underlying state of the world it describes.

nodes.label: Markov decision process
nodes.plain: States, actions, a transition rule and a reward — the whole formal object RL optimises inside.

nodes.label: Policy
nodes.plain: A rule mapping states to actions, or to a distribution over actions.

nodes.label: Discount factor
nodes.plain: Gamma: how much a reward one step later is worth, which also keeps infinite-horizon returns finite.

nodes.label: Value function
nodes.plain: The expected discounted return from a state, following a given policy.

nodes.label: Q-value
nodes.plain: The expected return from taking one specific action in a state and following the policy afterwards.

nodes.label: Bellman equation
nodes.plain: A value equals the immediate reward plus the discounted value of where you land — the recursion everything else is a way of solving.

nodes.label: Policy evaluation
nodes.plain: Compute the value of a fixed policy by iterating the Bellman equation to a fixed point.

nodes.label: Policy improvement
nodes.plain: Given values, take the greedy action in every state — the new policy is never worse.

nodes.label: Policy iteration
nodes.plain: Alternate evaluation and improvement until the policy stops changing.

nodes.label: TD error
nodes.plain: The gap between your current value estimate and reward-plus-next-estimate — the learning signal for every bootstrapping method.

nodes.label: Epsilon-greedy
nodes.plain: Take the greedy action most of the time and a random one with probability epsilon, so you keep exploring.

nodes.label: Q-learning
nodes.plain: Update towards the reward plus the best next Q-value, regardless of what you actually did next.

nodes.label: SARSA
nodes.plain: Update towards the reward plus the Q-value of the action you actually took next.

nodes.label: Eligibility traces
nodes.plain: Credit not just the last state but a decaying trail of recent ones, controlled by lambda.

nodes.label: Multi-armed bandit
nodes.plain: A one-state MDP: pull arms, learn which pays best, trade exploration against exploitation.

nodes.label: UCB selection
nodes.plain: Pick the arm with the best optimistic estimate — mean plus a bonus that shrinks as you sample it more.

nodes.label: DQN
nodes.plain: Q-learning where the Q-table is replaced by a neural network, stabilised by a replay buffer and a target network.

nodes.label: Q-network
nodes.plain: The network mapping a state to one Q-value per action.

nodes.label: Replay buffer
nodes.plain: Store past transitions and train on random samples, breaking the correlation between consecutive steps.

nodes.label: Target network
nodes.plain: A frozen copy of the Q-network used to compute the bootstrap target, updated only occasionally.

nodes.label: Probe environments
nodes.plain: Tiny hand-made environments with known correct value functions, run before the real one.

nodes.label: Policy gradient theorem
nodes.plain: The gradient of expected return equals the expected return-weighted gradient of the log-probability of the actions you took.

nodes.label: REINFORCE
nodes.plain: Sample a trajectory, weight each action's log-probability by the return that followed it, step.

nodes.label: Rollout buffer
nodes.plain: Storage for one batch of on-policy experience, discarded after the update.

nodes.label: Baseline subtraction
nodes.plain: Subtract a state-dependent constant from the return; the gradient is unchanged in expectation but much lower variance.

nodes.label: Entropy bonus
nodes.plain: Add the policy's entropy to the objective so it doesn't collapse to a single action too early.

nodes.label: Actor–critic
nodes.plain: Two heads: one that picks actions and one that estimates value, trained together.

nodes.label: Advantage
nodes.plain: How much better an action was than the policy's average from that state.

nodes.label: Generalized advantage estimation (GAE)
nodes.plain: A lambda-weighted sum of TD residuals that slides between one-step (biased, low variance) and full-return (unbiased, high variance) advantage estimates.

nodes.label: PPO
nodes.plain: Take several gradient steps on one batch of experience, using a clipped objective to stop the policy moving too far.

nodes.label: Clipped surrogate objective
nodes.plain: Clip the probability ratio to [1-eps, 1+eps] so that once an update has moved far enough the gradient goes flat.

nodes.label: Value-function loss
nodes.plain: The critic's own regression target — squared error against the observed returns.

nodes.label: Trust region (TRPO)
nodes.plain: Constrain each update to a KL ball around the old policy so it can't move somewhere the advantage estimates don't apply.

nodes.label: Reward shaping
nodes.plain: Add extra reward terms to make a sparse objective learnable.

nodes.label: Reward hacking
nodes.plain: The agent maximises the metric you wrote instead of the outcome you meant.

nodes.label: RLHF
nodes.plain: Fine-tune a language model with PPO against a learned reward model, keeping it close to a frozen copy of itself.

nodes.label: Reward model
nodes.plain: A model trained on human preference comparisons that scores a completion — a stand-in for a judgement you can't write down.

nodes.label: Value head
nodes.plain: A second output head bolted onto the language model to serve as PPO's critic.

nodes.label: RLHF KL penalty
nodes.plain: A per-token penalty on how far the policy's distribution has moved from the frozen reference model.

nodes.label: Reference model
nodes.plain: The frozen pre-RLHF copy the KL penalty is measured against.

nodes.label: Mode collapse
nodes.plain: The policy narrows onto a small set of high-reward phrasings and stops producing anything else.

nodes.label: LoRA
nodes.plain: Freeze the base weights and train a pair of low-rank matrices alongside them, so fine-tuning costs a fraction of the memory.

nodes.label: GRPO
nodes.plain: A PPO variant for LLMs that drops the critic and uses the mean reward across several rollouts of the same prompt as the baseline.

nodes.label: Monte Carlo tree search
nodes.plain: Select, expand, evaluate, back up: build a search tree biased toward promising moves.

nodes.label: PUCT
nodes.plain: The selection rule that balances a child's current value against a prior-weighted exploration bonus.

nodes.label: AlphaZero
nodes.plain: A policy-and-value network guiding MCTS, trained on games it plays against itself.

nodes.label: Self-play
nodes.plain: Generate training data by playing the current network against itself, so the opposition improves as you do.

nodes.label: Threat model & specification
nodes.plain: Write down the real-world harm and the causal chain to it, then pin the fuzzy word to something you can actually measure.

nodes.label: Alignment faking
nodes.plain: A model behaves well when it believes it is being trained or watched, and differently when it believes it is not.

nodes.label: Eval question design
nodes.plain: The wording of a question is part of the measurement; small changes move the number more than the property does.

nodes.label: Model-written dataset generation
nodes.plain: Use a model to write the eval questions, then use another to score and filter them.

nodes.label: Structured output
nodes.plain: Force the generator into a schema so the questions come back parseable rather than prose.

nodes.label: Few-shot prompting
nodes.plain: Show examples in the prompt to fix the format and the difficulty of what comes back.

nodes.label: Variance prompts
nodes.plain: Deliberately perturb the generation prompt so the dataset doesn't collapse into near-duplicates.

nodes.label: LLM scorer
nodes.plain: A model grading generated questions against a rubric before they enter the dataset.

nodes.label: Inspect
nodes.plain: The UK AISI evals framework: datasets, solvers, scorers and logs assembled into a Task.

nodes.label: Solver
nodes.plain: A composable step that transforms the conversation state — templating a prompt, formatting choices, asking for self-critique.

nodes.label: Scorer
nodes.plain: The function that turns a model's answer into a graded result.

nodes.label: Task
nodes.plain: Dataset plus solver chain plus scorer — the unit Inspect actually runs.

nodes.label: LLM agent
nodes.plain: A model in a loop with tools and an environment, choosing its own next action.

nodes.label: Tool use
nodes.plain: Give the model callable functions with schemas and let it decide when to call them.

nodes.label: ReAct
nodes.plain: Alternate an explicit reasoning step with an action step, so the model plans before it acts.

nodes.label: AI control
nodes.plain: Assume the model may be trying to subvert you, and design a protocol that stays safe anyway.

nodes.label: Backdoor
nodes.plain: Code that passes the tests but fails on a specific input the attacker chose.

nodes.label: Trusted monitoring
nodes.plain: A weaker but trusted model reads the untrusted model's output and rates how suspicious it looks.

nodes.label: Suspiciousness score
nodes.plain: The monitor's numeric output, and the threshold on it that decides what gets audited.

nodes.label: Upfront auditing
nodes.plain: Spend the human audit budget on the first N submissions and accept everything afterwards.

nodes.label: Defer to trusted
nodes.plain: When suspicion crosses the threshold, throw away the untrusted output and use the trusted model's instead.

nodes.label: Trusted editing
nodes.plain: Let the trusted model rewrite the suspicious parts rather than discarding the whole answer.

nodes.label: Safety–usefulness frontier
nodes.plain: Every protocol trades catching backdoors against throwing away good work; the comparison is a curve, not a number.

nodes.label: Emergent misalignment
nodes.plain: Fine-tuning on one narrow bad behaviour produces broadly misaligned behaviour across unrelated domains.

nodes.label: Model organism
nodes.plain: A model deliberately trained to have the property you want to study, so you can study it at all.

nodes.label: Autorater
nodes.plain: An LLM grading free-text model outputs against a written rubric, standing in for a human rater.

nodes.label: Contrastive steering vector
nodes.plain: Take the difference of mean activations between aligned and misaligned responses and steer along it.

nodes.label: Misalignment phase transition
nodes.plain: During narrow fine-tuning the general misaligned solution appears abruptly rather than gradually.

nodes.label: Agentic misalignment testbed
nodes.plain: A simulated shell environment where a model with a goal can take actions its operators would not sanction.

nodes.label: Shutdown resistance
nodes.plain: Testing whether a model given a task will disable or evade a mechanism that would stop it.

nodes.label: Scratchpad reasoning
nodes.plain: Give the model a private-seeming place to think and read what it says there — with the caveat that it may not reflect the real computation.

nodes.label: Red-teaming your own result
nodes.plain: Before believing a misalignment finding, try to produce it from a confound.

nodes.label: Thought anchor
nodes.plain: A sentence in a reasoning trace that disproportionately shapes everything after it.

nodes.label: Resampling importance
nodes.plain: Regenerate the trace from a given sentence many times and measure how much the final answer distribution moves.

nodes.label: Counterfactual importance
nodes.plain: Replace one sentence with an alternative and measure the change in the answer.

nodes.label: Receiver head
nodes.plain: An attention head that pulls information from reasoning steps into the final answer position.

nodes.label: Chain-of-thought faithfulness
nodes.plain: Whether the stated reasoning is the reasoning the model actually used.

nodes.label: Persona vector
nodes.plain: A direction in activation space corresponding to a personality trait, extracted from contrastive responses.

nodes.label: Assistant axis
nodes.plain: The principal direction in persona space along which the Assistant character sits.

nodes.label: Activation capping
nodes.plain: Find the normal activation range along the Assistant axis and clamp the model when it would exceed it.

nodes.label: Persona drift
nodes.plain: A long conversation walking the model away from the Assistant persona, one turn at a time.

nodes.label: Projection monitoring
nodes.plain: Project live activations onto a trait vector to watch a behaviour appear before it shows up in the text.

nodes.label: Investigator agent
nodes.plain: An LLM that probes another model over many turns, finding behaviours single-turn evals miss.

nodes.label: Petri
nodes.plain: Anthropic's open framework for automated auditing: an auditor agent, a target, and a judge, run at scale.

nodes.label: Red-team campaign
nodes.plain: Run many adversarial conversations in parallel and grade them against a rubric.

nodes.label: Sandbagging
nodes.plain: A model underperforming on purpose when it detects it is being evaluated.

nodes.label: Capstone project
nodes.plain: One question, small enough to answer in three Saturdays, using a technique you have already implemented.

nodes.label: Paper replication
nodes.plain: Reproduce one figure from one paper, then say one honest thing about what it does and doesn't show.

nodes.label: Final presentation
nodes.plain: 12 December 2026 — the talk that, with 11 of 14 Saturdays attended, is the pass condition.
